topic: The Toeplitz's Conjecture: Can we always inscribe a square in any closed loop?

sections.title: The Visual Hook: The Inscribed Square Problem
lecture_lines: Can we inscribe a square in any closed loop?
Consider a smooth, continuous, non-self-intersecting curve.
Even for irregular loops, a square often exists.
animations: Display a curve with an inscribed quadrilateral. Color #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/loop.svg]
Highlight the four vertices of the quadrilateral, color #FF0000.
Flash the vertices when they form a square, #00FF00. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/loop.svg]

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Configuration Spaces
lecture_lines: We analyze the space of all point pairs.
Map curve points to a 2D configuration grid.
This space helps simplify our complex geometry problem.
animations: Display a point-pair space grid using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg], color #FFFFFF.
Trace a path between points using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/path.svg] with color #FFFF00.
Highlight the intersection area using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/intersection.svg] with color #00FFFF.

sections.title: Mathematical Core: Symmetry and the Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
lecture_lines: Borsuk-Ulam theorem is our logical bridge.
It links sphere points to plane values.
It proves existence by mapping to zero.
Symmetry helps us identify the square's corners.
This confirms a square must always exist.
animations: Display a torus surface representation in color #FFFFFF using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/torus.svg].
Highlight antipodal points on the torus, color #FF0000.
Show the mapping function paths, color #00FFFF.
Flash the intersecting antipodal point, color #00FF00.
Overlay the square formation logic, color #FFFF00 using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/torus.svg].

sections.title: The Proof Logic: Connecting Vertices
lecture_lines: Define a function based on point-pair distance.
Construct squares using midpoint and distance.
The non-square configurations form an inconsistent set.
This logic forces a perfect square solution.
The square snaps onto the curve's perimeter.
animations: Display the function graph for point pairs, color #FFFFFF.
Show the geometric construction path, color #FFFF00.
Flash the final perfect square [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] intersection, color #00FF00.
Confirm the square [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] alignment on the curve, #FF00FF.
Snap the square [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] into its final position, #00FFFF.

sections.title: Application & Conclusion
lecture_lines: Toeplitz's Conjecture remains open for general curves.
Topology provides certainty beyond simple trial-error.
Mathematics guarantees success for these shapes.

Scale a square [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] to fit the polygon, color #FFFF00.
Flash the final inscribed square [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg], color #00FF00.
